name: Bala
origin: West African gourd-resonated xylophone (Guinea, Senegal, Mali).

name: Bodhran Saxum
origin: An Irish frame drum with a single membrane.

name: Bongo
origin: Afro-Cuban; a pair of open bottomed drums played with both hands.

name: Marimba
origin: Percussion musical instrument popular in Guatemala and other Central and NW South American countries; wooden bars with pipe or gourd resonators, struck by yarn wrapped or rubber mallets. Originally developed in Africa.  Marimba was proclaimed the national instrument of Guatemala in its independence proclamation.

name: Msondo
origin: Tanzania; tall cylindrically shaped drum for important rituals, which “drives” the dance.

name: Naqqara
origin: Drum of the Near and Middle East (Iraq, Iran, Turkey), and India; pair of clay or metal kettle drums of various sizes played with curved beaters.

name: Puniu Saxum
origin: Hawaiian small drum with a coconut body and a single sharkskin or fishskin head laced to the bottom.

name: Tamboril
origin: Uruguay; barrel-shaped drum used to play the Candombe music, a style created by African slaves.
